summary: Updates the RELATED-TO property of iCalendar (RFC 5545) with new relation types and adds the LINK, CONCEPT, and REFID properties. Together these let calendar items be linked to each other and to related data, and be grouped more flexibly. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: Calendar events usually sit alone. This adds sticky notes saying this event goes with that one, or links to files, so related events can be tied together.

subtitle: New ways for calendar events and tasks to point at each other, share a group key, and link to outside resources.

tldr.problem: iCalendar items often need to relate to each other or to outside data, but RELATED-TO had no timing relationships, CATEGORIES is only free-form tagging, and there was no general way to reference external information.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds temporal and ordering RELTYPE values, a GAP parameter and URI values for RELATED-TO, plus three properties: LINK, CONCEPT and REFID.
tldr.outcome: Calendar components can now express project-style dependencies, be grouped by a key, be categorized by a reference, and carry typed links. It updates the RELATED-TO definition in RFC 5545.

today: RFC 9253 is a Proposed Standard from August 2022. It updates RFC 5545 by replacing its RELATED-TO definition, and no later RFC obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Three Kinds of Relationship
sections.content:
iCalendar entities from RFC 5545 often need to be related to each other or to metadata. This RFC supports three forms. Structured relationships are things like parent, sibling, before or after. Grouped relationships tie entities together as a set. Linked relationships point to other entities, such as vCards, through a URI with REL and FMTTYPE parameters.

Grouping was previously done with CATEGORIES, which the RFC calls problematic for developers because it is inconsistent and used as a free-form tag.

It also says a calendar entity should generally be understandable without downloading what it references. To support offline display, a link type may mark important data to download in advance.
sections.plainLanguage: Events can be related as family (parent and child), as a team, or by pointing at something else, like a phone number card.

sections.title: Temporal and Ordering Relationship Types
sections.content:
The RELTYPE parameter of RELATED-TO gets four temporal values: FINISHTOSTART, FINISHTOFINISH, STARTTOFINISH and STARTTOSTART. The RELATED-TO property sits on the predecessor (Task-A) and refers to the successor (Task-B). For example, with FINISHTOSTART, Task-B cannot start until Task-A finishes: when painting is complete, carpet laying can begin.

Five further values are added. FIRST and NEXT describe position in a series. DEPENDS-ON says the current component depends on the referenced one, for instance a task blocked on another. REFID and CONCEPT reference components that carry a matching REFID or CONCEPT property. PARENT, CHILD and SIBLING stay hierarchical, while FIRST and NEXT are ordering relationships.
sections.plainLanguage: Painting must finish before carpet goes down. These labels let a calendar say things like finish-then-start, or what comes first and next.

sections.title: The GAP and LINKREL Parameters
sections.content:
The GAP parameter may be placed on RELATED-TO and holds a duration (the dur-value of RFC 5545). Positive means lag time between a task and its successor, negative means lead time. The RFC's example is painting a room, then laying carpet after a gap of 1 day so the paint can dry.

The LINKREL parameter MUST be present on every LINK property and says what kind of reference it is. Its value is a quoted URI or a registered token from the Web Linking registry (RFC 8288). There is no default relation type. The RFC gives latest-version as an example, meaning the latest version of the event information.

Two new value types for the VALUE parameter are also defined: UID, a component's unique identifier, and XML-REFERENCE, a URI with an XPointer anchor for a fragment of an XML document.
sections.plainLanguage: A gap is the waiting time between two jobs, like letting paint dry for a day. The link label tells you why a link is there.

sections.title: The New Properties: LINK, CONCEPT and REFID
sections.content:
LINK gives a reference to external information related to a component. Its value is a URI, a UID or an XML-REFERENCE, and the VALUE parameter is required. It serializes the Web Linking model of RFC 8288: LABEL maps to the title attribute, LANGUAGE to hreflang, LINKREL to the relation type and FMTTYPE to type. It MUST NOT be treated as just another attachment. A UID value must name a component in the same collection, and may need replacing by a URI on import.

CONCEPT holds a URI that names a formal category, as opposed to the informal tags of CATEGORIES. The name comes from SKOS, and structured URIs allow hierarchical categorization. REFID is free-form text used as a key: all components with the same REFID are associated and can be retrieved as a group, such as all events of a travel itinerary. Unlike CONCEPT, a REFID adds no meaning to the component.

All three can appear zero or more times in any iCalendar component.
sections.plainLanguage: LINK is a signpost to a web page or another event. CONCEPT is an official category label. REFID is a shared folder name that puts related items together.

sections.title: Changes to RELATED-TO
sections.content:
Section 9.1 replaces the RELATED-TO definition in Section 3.8.4.5 of RFC 5545. RELATED-TO may now hold a URI, a UID or TEXT, and accepts a GAP parameter. By default the value points to a component with a PARENT relationship, and RELTYPE can switch this to CHILD, SIBLING or a temporal relationship.

To preserve backwards compatibility, the value type MUST be UID when PARENT, SIBLING or CHILD is used. The RFC notes that this property only describes relationships. Changes to a referenced component can have implicit effects on related ones, and it is up to the target calendar system to maintain those implications. Deleting a target can leave broken links.
sections.plainLanguage: The old note-linking tool got upgrades, but the old simple uses still work the same way.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
All the security considerations of Section 7 of RFC 5545 apply. Applications using LINK must be aware of the risks of the URIs they are given, and the RFC points out that referenced resources carry no stability guarantee (RFC 3986).

XML-REFERENCE targets are XML, so consumers need to be aware of XML entity issues. The reference may also be invalid or become so over time. CONCEPT and the redefined RELATED-TO have the same URI issues, and extremely large GAP values may lead to unexpected behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: A link can lead somewhere unsafe or somewhere that has since disappeared, so apps should be careful when following them.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA added the properties CONCEPT, LINK and REFID to the iCalendar property registry and added this document as a reference for RELATED-TO. It registered the parameters GAP and LINKREL, the value data types UID and XML-REFERENCE, and nine relationship types: CONCEPT, DEPENDS-ON, FINISHTOFINISH, FINISHTOSTART, FIRST, NEXT, REFID, STARTTOFINISH and STARTTOSTART.
sections.plainLanguage: All the new words were written down in the official iCalendar dictionary so everyone spells them the same way.

items.label: Finish-to-start
items.desc: Task-B cannot start until Task-A finishes.

items.label: Finish-to-finish
items.desc: Task-B can only be completed after Task-A is finished.

items.label: Start-to-finish
items.desc: The start of Task-A controls the finish of Task-B.

items.label: Start-to-start
items.desc: Task-B can start anytime after Task-A starts.

items.label: First in series
items.desc: Referenced component is first in the series.

items.label: Next in series
items.desc: Referenced component is next in the series.

items.label: Depends on
items.desc: Current component depends on the referenced one.

items.label: Reference by REFID
items.desc: Refers to components with a matching REFID property.

items.label: Reference by CONCEPT
items.desc: Refers to components with a matching CONCEPT property.
